overall: The AG found the Council President violated the Open Meeting Law by directing that a second Zoom link used to transmit an open committee meeting be disabled; the deliberation claim failed and the subcommittees were not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Council President allegedly deliberated by emailing all Councilors a letter about remote participation rules for a committee meeting, outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Although the letter was sent to all Councilors, we do not find such communication to be deliberation as the letter simply memorialized advice from Assistant City Solicitor McNeil.

allegations.summary: Council President allegedly restricted a person's right to transmit a Parks and Recreation Committee meeting by having remote access links disabled during the June 28 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that President Spadafora violated the Open Meeting Law by directing that the second Zoom link set up by Chair O’Malley to transmit the June 28 meeting be disabled.

allegations.summary: Complaint named two subcommittees as violators but listed no specific allegations against them, so the AG limited review to the Council.
allegations.key_passage: there does not appear to be any specific allegations listed in the complaint against the Parks and Recreation Committee or the Committee on Technology and Policy.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
